chapter: Wagon bands, halls and the old brass bands
title: Bunk Johnson and the rough Irish Channel gang
summary: Bunk disappeared for a gig with a rowdy Irish longshoremen's gang led by Eddie Halliday.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: He disappeared, huh. Where did he...

He went with the circus. He took some money for a gig with some Irishmen on the waterfront, that Jefferson City Buffet(?) Gang. They was a bad, rough gang of Irishmen who acted like Negroes and danced like Negroes, who could jump just like the Negroes, they'd act like Negroes, and they was rough and rowdy, and they fought -- they're still up there now in the Irish Channel. They work hard, and they do all the...all the work just above the work that they would give Negroes. Driving trucks, they got the

gangs on the riverfront, they're foremen... And Eddie Halliday, a tough Irishman who would pull his coat off and fight, and one got the gang...you know, test Eddie Halliday's Negroes, you know, insult them on the river, because Eddie Halliday would come over there and cap the joint.
